verdict_context.what: TASK-140 §1.A.3: a verdict is only attributable together with the window budget it was measured at and the round (independent complete run) it came from; TASK-139 measured that w30 verdicts were not reproducible across rounds, so a bare verdict string is not evidence of a class

reporting_window.declared_by: TASK-139 §1.A: the minimum.  TASK-140 §1.A.1: the reporting window.
reporting_window.basis: MEASURED (TASK-139 §A.4: three complete w30 probes and two complete w90 probes of the same five games, same command, same code): at w30 the per-game verdict was NOT reproducible across rounds -- asteroids, tetris, pong and breakout each changed class between rounds (4 of 5), with the mechanism located per step (Engine.get_frames_drawn() span jitter plus an occasionally missing ack_result); at w90 the two complete rounds agreed per game on the same five games.  The reporting window is therefore 90: below it a verdict is still measured, still recorded and still printed, but it is a REFERENCE reading and can never count as a pass.
reporting_window.rule: TASK-140 §1.A.1: a verdict produced at a nominal `--window-frames` below the declared reporting window is REPORTED (as reference) and can never be a PASS.  It is a statement about the MEASUREMENT's reproducibility -- TASK-139 measured that w30 verdicts changed class between rounds for the same command and the same code, while w90's did not.
not_a_loosening: the check can only take a run OUT of PASS, never put one in
it does not change `--window-frames`, `min_frames`, or either ruler's formula
a run at or above the reporting window is byte-for-byte unaffected
